description: Multi-dimensional adversarial review of a diff or capability: correctness, security, and spec compliance, with every finding adversarially verified before it is reported.

findings.title: Missions completed by a task-side admin change never get their completion bonus
findings.evidence: `PublishedMissionChanged` is only published from `MissionService.edit` and `MissionService.setStatus` (MissionService.kt:73, :89). A served mission's task list also shrinks when a task is deleted (`TaskService.delete` → `missions.removeTask(id)`, line 150), unpublished (`TaskService.setStatus`, line 156), or made unservable some other way, because `ServedContentService.served` drops non-PUBLISHED/non-TEXT tasks. If the removed task was the mission's last unresolved one, the mission is now complete but no event fires. `Gamification.onAttempt` only pays bonuses on a new primary resolution, and no task in that mission can be resolved any more, so the bonus is never paid unless an admin happens to re-save the mission. The design (decision 4, OQ-28) says that removing the last unresolved task completes the mission 'the same way'.
findings.suggestion: Publish `PublishedMissionChanged` (or a broader `ServedMissionsChanged`) for every published mission affected by a task delete, status change or modality change in TaskService. One option is to have `removeTask` return the affected mission ids, which it already collects. Add an IT that deletes or unpublishes the last unresolved task and checks that the bonus row is written.

findings.title: Briefing xpAvailable offers the mission bonus for a complete mission that has no bonus row
findings.evidence: `available()` returns `open * config.xp.firstAttempt + if (paid) 0 else config.xp.missionBonus` and never checks whether the mission is already complete. Design decision 8 says xpAvailable is '0 for a complete mission and during a replay'. A complete mission with no bonus row will therefore show 20 XP available that can never be earned (replays earn nothing). This happens when the task-side change above completes a mission, and for missions completed in the primary scope before V5. The child sees XP on offer that will never be awarded.
findings.suggestion: Add the bonus only when `open > 0`, or when `!complete(mission)`. Better still, also fix the missing-bonus paths so a complete, unpaid mission cannot exist.

findings.title: No ledger backfill for primary-scope resolutions and completed missions from before V5
findings.evidence: V5 creates an empty `xp_award` table. `Gamification.onAttempt` awards XP only on a new resolving attempt (`state.resolved` after the insert), and `complete()` is only evaluated for missions containing the task just resolved. Any task resolved, or mission completed, under slice 7 therefore never earns XP or its bonus. HQ shows `totalXp` 0 next to a non-zero `solvedTasks`. If a deployed database already has slice-7 attempts, this is effectively lost XP (FR-38).
findings.suggestion: Confirm whether any deployed data predates V5. If it does, add an append-only backfill: a new migration, or a startup task under the practice lock. It should insert TASK rows for each first primary resolution (using `hints_used`) and MISSION_BONUS rows for served missions that are already complete. If no such data exists, record that decision in design.md.

findings.title: Admin publish/edit now fails if the synchronous gamification listener throws
findings.evidence: `onPublishedMissionChanged` is a plain `@EventListener` running inside the admin's content transaction. It takes the practice advisory lock, reads every primary attempt for the mission and inserts a ledger row. Any exception it raises propagates out of `events.publishEvent(...)` in `MissionService.setStatus`/`edit`, so the admin's publish fails and rolls back, probably as a generic 500. Examples are a unique-index violation if an invariant is ever broken, or a row rejected by `CHECK amount`. The content module now depends at runtime on practice for its own writes to succeed.
findings.suggestion: This coupling may be what you want, since the bonus is atomic with the publish. If so, map any listener failure to an RFC 7807 response with a human-readable message, or use an idempotent insert (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` on the partial unique index) so a race cannot block publishing.

findings.title: Summary's completing attempt re-implements resolution logic instead of using TaskProgress
findings.evidence: `.filter { it.correct || it.attemptNo == TaskProgress.MAX_ATTEMPTS }` restates the rule for when an attempt resolves a task, which `TaskProgress(...).state.resolved` already encodes. If resolution rules change (for example, more attempts or reveal-on-request), the summary's `completing` attempt, and with it `rankUp`, will silently drift from the state machine used everywhere else.
findings.suggestion: Derive the resolving attempt per task from `TaskProgress` (e.g. `groupBy taskId → TaskProgress(list).takeIf { state.resolved }?.latest`), then take the latest by `createdAt`.

findings.title: Every read and write reloads and sums the entire XP ledger several times per request
findings.evidence: `ofAttempt` calls `ledger.awards()` and filters it in memory. It runs for each `outcome()`, so for every task screen and every submit. `onAttempt`, `available`, `progress`, `acknowledge` and `summary` each load the full table again, and `progress` also queries `celebrated()`. A single submit loads the full ledger at least twice. The design accepts in-memory sums, but `ofAttempt` could use the existing `xp_award_attempt_idx`.
findings.suggestion: Add targeted port methods: `awardsOf(attemptId)`, `total()` as SQL `sum(amount)`, `bonusPaid(missionId)` and `taskAwarded(taskId)`. Keep `awards()` for the summary only.

findings.title: Unreadable config resource surfaces as a raw IOException rather than InvalidGamificationConfig
findings.evidence: Only `!resource.exists()` is mapped to `InvalidGamificationConfig`. If `doucko.gamification.config` points at an existing but unreadable path (a directory, or a file with denied permissions), `resource.inputStream` throws an IOException. That stops startup with a stack trace that does not name the key, contrary to the KDoc ('An unreadable or invalid file stops the start with [InvalidGamificationConfig] naming the key').
findings.suggestion: Check `resource.isReadable` and wrap the read in try/catch(IOException), rethrowing `InvalidGamificationConfig("doucko.gamification.config", "names no readable file")`.

findings.title: xpAvailable assumes firstAttempt is the maximum award, which is wrong when minimum > firstAttempt
findings.evidence: The parser accepts `firstAttempt` 0..1000 and `minimum` 1..1000 independently. `XpRules.taskAward` pays `maxOf(config.minimum, ...)`, so with e.g. `firstAttempt: 0, minimum: 5` each task earns 5, but `available()` computes `open * config.xp.firstAttempt` = 0. The same mismatch applies if `secondAttempt` or `revealed` is greater than `firstAttempt`.
findings.suggestion: Use `XpRules.taskAward(config.xp, CORRECT_FIRST_TRY, 0)`, or the maximum over states, as the per-task figure. Alternatively, add cross-field validation in the parser (minimum ≤ firstAttempt, secondAttempt ≤ firstAttempt) if the spec intends that ordering.

findings.title: COVERAGE SUMMARY: 16 delta scenarios: 16 implemented, 0 partial, 0 missing, 0 contradicted
findings.evidence: I traced each of the 16 delta scenarios to code and to a matching test. Award table, Neutral submissions and Hints/replays: Gamification.kt:63-83 and XpRules (domain/Gamification.kt:32-42), tested at GamificationIT.kt:210/242/266/377. Shared task, two missions and published-already-complete: Gamification.kt:74-80 and 95-104, plus the MissionService events, tested at GamificationIT.kt:401/424/459/486. Config keys, ladder and alternate file: GamificationConfigParser.kt, tested in GamificationConfigTest and GamificationConfigIT.kt:136/149. Mid-mission rank-up, pending rank-up with ack, and older ack: PracticeService submit, Gamification.acknowledge and progress(), tested at GamificationIT.kt:501/530/573. Summary/replay and available XP: RunXp.summarize and Gamification.available, tested at GamificationIT.kt:634/377/678. Append-only ledger and XP never goes down: V5 trigger, tested at GamificationIT.kt:695/707. Every FR assigned to this repo for slice 8 (FR-32..FR-39) appears in the delta spec and has @trace tests. No NFR travels with this slice. The OpenAPI fields used (AttemptResult xpAwarded/bonusXp/completedMissionIds/rankUp, HqView.pendingRankUp, Rank{index,name,minXp}, MissionBriefing.xpAvailable, MissionSummary xpEarned/rankUp/rankReachedDuringRun, ackRankUp 204/400) match contract/api/openapi.yaml. No new endpoints or status codes were added. Ticked tasks 1.1–4.2 all have their artifacts (V5__gamification.sql, the test classes, docs/qa/evidence/slice8-red-run.md, the domain types, PlaceholderLadder removed, PublishedMissionChanged, missionsContaining, JdbcXpLedger, gamification.json). Tasks 5.1–5.6 are honestly left unticked.
findings.suggestion: Nothing to fix here; this row is the coverage summary. Finish tasks 5.1–5.6 (qa:verify, openspec validate --strict, review-gate with review-findings.json, compose smoke, current-state, archive) before calling the slice done.

findings.title: Mid-mission rank-up is marked as played by the server on the POST response, but the store spec says a celebration counts as played only once the client acknowledges it
findings.evidence: The store spec contract/openspec/specs/gamification/spec.md:261 says: "A celebration counts as played once the client acknowledges it." The delta spec (line 92-93) says the opposite for AttemptResult.rankUp: "that celebration counts as played". OpenAPI AttemptResult.rankUp agrees with the delta ("one-shot: the POST response is its only carrier"). The code follows the delta and contract: `val rankUp = xp.crossing?.takeIf { !result.missionComplete }; rankUp?.let { gamification.celebrated(it, record.createdAt) }`. It writes rank_celebration with no client ack. So if the POST response is lost (tab closed or network drop), the mid-mission celebration never plays again. Under the store spec it would still be pending on HQ.
findings.suggestion: Amend the store spec (a docs-store change) so it says a mid-mission AttemptResult.rankUp is one-shot and counts as played when the response is sent, and that only mission-complete and out-of-session crossings need ackRankUp. The other option is to make mid-mission crossings pending until acknowledged as well, but that would also need a contract change.

findings.title: Undocumented rule: rank names are limited to 50 characters and duplicate JSON keys are refused
findings.evidence: The delta spec (line 63-69) says startup is refused only when "a rank name is missing or blank". It sets no length limit and says nothing about duplicate keys. The code also refuses names longer than NAME_MAX = 50 code points (`name.codePointCount(0, name.length) > NAME_MAX` → "must be a text of 1 to 50 characters"). It also turns on `StreamReadFeature.STRICT_DUPLICATE_DETECTION`, so a duplicated key makes the backend refuse to start. Neither rule comes from any requirement, and no scenario covers the 50-character limit.
findings.suggestion: Amend the delta spec (and the store spec's "Swappable skin"/"Rank ladder") to state the 1..50 character limit for rank names and that duplicate keys are refused, and add a boundary test for 50 and 51 characters. Or drop the limit if the spec isn't changed.

findings.title: Reloaded TaskView.lastFeedback now shows the stored XP of the last attempt and drops its rank-up; no requirement covers this
findings.evidence: The delta spec only covers XP in the POST AttemptResult, the summary, the briefing and HQ. The code also fills `lastFeedback` on GET task screens from the ledger (`xp = gamification.ofAttempt(latest.id)` in PracticeService.outcome) and forces `rankUp = null` (`lastFeedback = screen.lastResult?.let { attempt(it.copy(rankUp = null)) }`). The comment points to "design decision 9" in design.md, not to a spec requirement. It fits the schema (lastFeedback is an AttemptResult), but no scenario says reloaded feedback must repeat xpAwarded/bonusXp/completedMissionIds or never carry rankUp. No test asserting it was visible in the gamification test names.
findings.suggestion: Add a scenario to the delta spec (e.g. "Reloaded task feedback shows the stored award and no rank-up") and an IT that reloads the task after a crossing attempt and checks the XP fields and rankUp null.

I refuted this finding: the failure it describes is either prevented or already turned into a proper error response.

1. **Wrong line.** `Gamification.kt` has only 176 lines. The listener is at lines 95–104, not 411.

2. **The duplicate-row case can't happen.** The listener first takes the advisory lock (`store.lock()`). It then checks whether a MISSION_BONUS row already exists for the mission, and only inserts if none does. Every path that awards XP takes the same lock, so two writers cannot race past the check. The partial unique index `xp_award_bonus_once_uq` is only a backstop.

3. **The `CHECK amount` case can't happen either.** The column requires `amount BETWEEN 0 AND 1000`. The bonus is `config.xp.missionBonus`, and `GamificationConfigParser` refuses any value outside that range (`XP_MAX = 1000`) when the config is loaded. The shipped value is 20.

4. **It would not be a raw 500 anyway.** Both of the finding's examples raise `DataIntegrityViolationException`. `ContentProblemAdvice` has `@Order(HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE)` and covers `MissionController`. Its handler at lines 60–61 maps that exception to a 409 `content-conflict` problem response with a message from the catalog. An admin publish or edit therefore gets an RFC 7807 response with a readable message, not a generic 500.

5. **The coupling is intended.** OQ-28 wants the bonus written atomically with the publish, which a synchronous listener inside the content transaction provides. The finding itself concedes this may be wanted.

What remains is "some unexpected exception might happen", which applies to any code in the transaction. That is not a correctness bug in this code.

The location is cited wrong: Gamification.kt is only 176 lines long, and the listener is at line 97, not 411. The coupling is real. `onPublishedMissionChanged` is a synchronous `@EventListener` with `@Transactional` (REQUIRED), so it joins the admin's transaction, and an exception thrown there would fail the publish. But neither failure the finding names can actually happen:

1. **Unique-index violation from a race:** both writers to `xp_award` call `store.lock()` before their check-then-insert. That lock is `pg_advisory_xact_lock` in JdbcPracticeStore. `onAttempt` is called with the practice lock held (see the class doc), and `onPublishedMissionChanged` calls `store.lock()` itself on line 98. Both check whether the bonus was already paid under that same lock, so they run one after the other and cannot race. With no race, `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` has nothing to guard against.

2. **`CHECK (amount BETWEEN 0 AND 1000)` rejecting a row:** the amount is always `config.xp.missionBonus`. GamificationConfigParser checks every XP value at startup to be within 0..`XP_MAX` (1000) and refuses unknown or missing keys. A bad config stops the app from starting, so no publish request ever reaches this insert with an out-of-range value.

The only failures left are general ones, such as the database being unreachable or a lock timeout. Those would break any write in the admin transaction, not something this listener introduces. Making the bonus atomic with the publish is also the intended design (OQ-28, design.md). No real user or attacker can trigger the claimed failure.
